clue.text: Appropriate place for an actor to immerse himself

definitions.meaning: fitting someone's usual nature, as behaviour that is typical of them

definitions.text: place for an actor to immerse himself
definitions.meaning: a performer who stays fully inside the role he plays is said to be in this state

explanation.surface: Where should a method actor bury himself? Somewhere fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Typical behaviour is consistent with a person's nature, and an actor fully absorbed in a role is likewise inside that part.

clue.text: Furious because entire map is ruined

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked and broken up, so the letters of the two words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is livid because the whole map they were using has been spoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is ruined' scrambles ENTIRE and MAP together; 'because' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being furious is being in a fit of rage, an idiom for losing one's composure.

clue.text: Miss Clinton is in London

definitions.meaning: the daughter of Bill and Hillary Clinton bears this first name
a district of west London, home of a famous football club

explanation.surface: A former US President's daughter is visiting the British capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' links the two definitions: the Clinton daughter's name is also a London district.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Clinton's daughter shares her first name with the fashionable Thames-side borough area of west London.

clue.text: Corresponding to all the points in a circle

indicators.note: the compass letters are placed inside the run made by the other two pieces

parts.note: a ring is a circle
all four compass points: north, south, west and east

explanation.surface: Something matching every one of the points around a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all the points' means every point of the compass, not points scored; 'in' does the container work. 'Corresponding' means matching, as one part answers to another.
explanation.definitionFit: Something answering to another thing matches or corresponds with it, as in a description fitting a suspect.

clue.text: A couple of attempts over and above

indicators.note: a couple means two, so the attempt word is written twice in a row

parts.note: a go is an attempt or try

explanation.surface: Two tries made in addition to what was required.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase, from French, means in abundance, so in excess or over and above what is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French, the phrase means in plenty, galore, surplus to what is needed.

clue.text: A chirpy speaker

parts.note: reads as a cheerful talker or a twittering bird, but means a small loudspeaker for high notes

explanation.definitionFit: This hi-fi loudspeaker handles high frequencies, and a bird that chirps could be named the same way.

clue.text: Army men get a word of thanks for producing a lasso

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: Soldiers are thanked for making a cowboy's rope.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for 'thank you'. The answer is a lariat, a word from Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a rope with a running noose used for catching livestock, chiefly in the American West.

clue.text: Church has entered the hunt

indicators.note: the word has goes into the church abbreviation, splitting it

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A congregation has joined the fox hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church' is the usual crossword abbreviation for the Church of England; 'the hunt' is the definition, with 'the' part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A chase is a pursuit, the hunting of quarry.

clue.text: Dispute results from angry talk about Sunday opening

indicators.note: the angry words go around the letter picked from the day of the week

parts.note: cross words are words spoken in anger

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A row follows a heated exchange at the start of the Sabbath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts CROSS WORDS around S, the first letter of Sunday ('opening'). 'results from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross swords is an idiom for quarrelling or arguing with someone.

clue.text: Jackson means to bat with caution

definitions.meaning: Thomas Jackson, the American Civil War Confederate general, had this nickname
in cricket, to play purely defensively, blocking every ball

explanation.surface: A man named Jackson intends to play defensively at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'means' links the definitions. In cricket the verb means batting only to survive, not to score.
explanation.definitionFit: General Thomas Jackson earned the nickname at Bull Run, and the word also names stubborn defensive batting or obstruction.

clue.text: Very quickly appreciate gusty weather

parts.note: to appreciate something is to like it
gusts are blasts of moving air

explanation.surface: Someone quickly comes to enjoy blustery conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving with the speed of a gale is an idiom for going very fast.

clue.text: Manage to define episcopal jurisdiction?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a bishop's authority lies above his diocese

explanation.surface: Does running things mean marking out a bishop's area?
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; the question mark flags the split reading of being in charge over it.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise is to direct work, and a bishop has authority over his see, or diocese.

clue.text: Two-way ticket to the wilds of Oz

parts.note: a return ticket takes you out and brings you back
the second half of the journey on a return ticket is the trip home

explanation.surface: A return fare to the Australian bush.
explanation.walkthrough: A two-way ticket is an 'out and back' fare. Oz is slang for Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the remote, sparsely populated interior of Australia.

clue.text: A shade sanctimonious in the main

indicators.note: the pious abbreviation sits inside the ocean word

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the open sea
pi is informal for piously self-righteous

explanation.surface: Someone a little holier-than-thou is out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A shade' looks like 'slightly', describing 'sanctimonious', but it is the definition: a brown colour.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a reddish-brown colour, originally from cuttlefish ink.

clue.text: Tense declaration of total self-satisfaction

definitions.meaning: in grammar, a verb form for an incomplete or continuing past action
a boast that one has no flaws at all, split as I'm and a word for flawless

explanation.surface: A tense statement of utter smugness.
explanation.walkthrough: The grammatical past tense of 'I was walking' shares its letters with the smug claim 'I'm flawless'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar names the continuous past form this way, and the smug boast claims to be flawless.

clue.text: He steals a saddle in cleaner enclosure

indicators.note: the cut of meat is placed inside the word for cleaner

parts.note: purer means cleaner, less contaminated
a saddle of lamb is a joint containing the loin

explanation.surface: A thief keeps a saddle in an enclosure for cleaning.
explanation.walkthrough: A saddle of meat is the double loin, so 'saddle' gives LOIN. 'a' and 'enclosure' fill out the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To purloin is to steal, so this is a thief.

clue.text: Issuing forth to back a Levantine country

annotationWithheld.clue: Issuing forth to back a Levantine country

clue.text: Become heated on German jingoist

parts.note: to warm is to grow hotter

explanation.surface: A patriot gets angry at a German.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who agitates for war is an aggressive nationalist, a jingoist.

clue.text: Circular motor in a musical instrument

parts.note: O is circular in shape
a motor is a car

explanation.surface: A round engine inside an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes.

clue.text: Beg for cocaine before Acid-House party

indicators.note: the drug letter comes before the party word

parts.note: C is slang for cocaine
a rave is a large dance party with acid-house music

explanation.surface: Someone pleads for drugs before a dance event.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg for something is to long for it intensely.

clue.text: I burst into song over one Tuscan wine

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits over, or above, the next
the letter I forces its way inside the song word

parts.note: a chant is a song
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone breaks into song while holding a glass of red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burst into' puts I inside CHANT; 'over' sets that above I (one) in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a red wine from Tuscany in Italy.

clue.text: Salesman gets fed up with programmes seen before

parts.note: rep is short for sales representative
read as eats up, consuming food

explanation.surface: A salesman is sick of reruns on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets fed up' reads as boredom but means 'eats'. Repeats are TV programmes shown again.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasts shown a second time are reruns.

clue.text: Variety of pearl a shade less dark

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters of the gem word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kind of pearl is somewhat lighter in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lighter in colour is comparatively whiter or fainter.

clue.text: Fight a little bit

explanation.definitionFit: A brawl is a minor scuffle in informal speech, and a fragment is a tiny piece of something.

clue.text: Old Baltic capital noted for Japanese art

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia
mi is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An ancient Baltic city famous for oriental craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted' is read as 'a note', the sol-fa MI; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Japanese craft of folding paper into decorative shapes.

clue.text: Tommy gets no backing, but has to persevere

parts.note: Tommy Atkins is slang for a British private soldier

indicators.note: the word no is put in reverse order

explanation.surface: A British private gets no support but must keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy is old slang for a British infantryman. 'backing' turns NO into ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going despite difficulty is to persist doggedly.

clue.text: Diana represented the spirit of spring

indicators.note: presented again in a new form, so the goddess's name is rearranged

explanation.surface: The goddess Diana stood for the essence of springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' is a water source, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this is a water nymph living in a spring, river or lake.

clue.text: Disperse again to bring in part of the harvest

parts.note: to bring in a crop is to reap it
a portion is a part or share

explanation.surface: Redistribute to gather a share of the crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of the harvest' fills out the surface around 'bring in'; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To distribute or share out a second time is to allot anew.
